clue.text: £500 calling for mischief

parts.note: a monkey is British slang for five hundred pounds
one's calling is one's line of work or trade

explanation.surface: Someone's lucrative job turns out to be nothing but a sum of money paid for making trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'monkey' is old British slang for £500 (a 'pony' is £25).
explanation.definitionFit: Monkey business is an idiom for playful or dishonest trickery, the same as mischief.

clue.text: This devil will shatter the simple hopes

indicators.note: something shattered is broken into pieces, so the letters that follow are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: fourteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A demon is warned to be the one who dashes the modest dreams of ordinary people.
explanation.walkthrough: Mephistopheles is the devil to whom Faust sells his soul in the legend; the clue reads as a description of him too.
explanation.definitionFit: Mephistopheles is the named demon of the Faust legend, a literary example of a devil.

clue.text: Gift for discovering grip for feeding horses

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase: the answer is a bag used for feeding horses

parts.note: a nose for something is a knack for sniffing it out
a grip is an old word for a travelling bag or holdall

explanation.surface: A talented sleuth is praised alongside the feed sack hung on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grip' looks like a hold of the hand, but here it is the old name for a gladstone-type travel bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosebag is the canvas sack hung over a horse's head so it can eat its oats or hay.

clue.text: Primitive men let ale ferment

indicators.note: fermenting liquid bubbles and churns, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Cavemen allow their beer to brew, a picture of basic early brewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ferment' at the end reads as the verb the men allow; it is the signal to rearrange the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemental describes something basic, fundamental and raw, close to primitive in sense.

clue.text: Musical instrument turns a poet's head

definitions.text: Musical instrument turns a poet's head

parts.note: surface reading: an instrument so sweet it distracts a poet
setter's reading: in Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner the wedding guest hears this instrument playing loudly and is distracted

explanation.surface: A beautiful instrument charms and distracts a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: In Coleridge's poem the Wedding-Guest 'heard the loud bassoon' and beat his breast, his attention pulled away from the Mariner's tale.
explanation.definitionFit: The bassoon is a low-pitched woodwind member of the orchestra, played with a double reed.

clue.text: Wise Father Christmas nearly eating a pie

indicators.note: something eaten goes inside the eater, so the following words sit within
nearly means not quite all, so the last letter of the gift-bringer's name goes

parts.note: Santa Claus, the Christmas gift-bringer
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sage-like Santa is caught tucking into a mince pie on Christmas Eve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' acts on the gift-bringer's name before it does the eating; a pie is the natural thing for Santa to tuck into.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient is a literary adjective for having great wisdom or discernment.

clue.text: Cuts make more than one cooler

definitions.meaning: first meaning: small notches or ... in a surface
second meaning: a cooler is slang for a prison, and so is a nick, here in the plural

explanation.surface: Slices into something produce several chilling devices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' looks like a fridge, but both 'cooler' and 'nick' are British slang for a prison or police station.
explanation.definitionFit: Small cuts are nicks, and since prison slang calls a jail a nick, several jails are nicks too.

clue.text: Hole behind station needs a fill-in

indicators.note: behind says this part comes after the other in the finished word

parts.note: a stop is a station on a bus or train route
a gap is an opening or hole

explanation.surface: A hole behind a railway station needs filling in.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names the hole first but places it after the station.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap is a temporary substitute used until something permanent arrives, just like a fill-in.

clue.text: Betrothal needs new wife to absorb good game

parts.note: a betrothal is a marriage contract

indicators.note: to absorb is to take something in, so the following letter goes inside

parts.note: a bride is a newly married woman
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: An engagement means a newly married woman must take in some good advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Contract bridge is the standard modern form of the card game bridge, with bidding to set a contract.

clue.text: Law enforcers at Sunday school in control

definitions.note: the clue word is read as a verb, to have in one's power, matching the verb answer

parts.note: a posse is a band summoned by a sheriff to enforce the law
SS is the abbreviation for Sunday school

explanation.surface: Sheriff's deputies attend Sunday school and take charge of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess something is to have it in your control or ownership, as in possessing land.

clue.text: Myopic coloratura uses a flute

indicators.note: uses suggests the words on the left employ, and so contain, what is wanted

parts.note: letters spanning the join between the two words

explanation.surface: A short-sighted opera singer is accompanied by a flute.
explanation.walkthrough: A coloratura is a soprano who sings elaborate runs; the instrument sits inside 'myoPIC COLOratura'.
explanation.definitionFit: The piccolo is the small, high-pitched member of the flute family.

clue.text: I am to be covering uncleês head in dye

parts.note: contracted to I'm

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so one piece sits outside the other

parts.note: the verb itself

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of uncle

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to wear something over their uncle's head while it is being coloured.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue is to saturate or stain fabric thoroughly with colour, as dyeing does.

clue.text: Mistake in supervision

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an error from failing to notice something
second meaning: watching over or managing others

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a single blunder by a manager; the two halves are opposite senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means both an unintentional slip and the act of watching over work, two nearly opposite senses.

clue.text: Mean fool, one hears, but well organised

parts.note: tight means stingy with money

indicators.note: one hears means what is listened to, so it is the sound of the word that counts

parts.note: a nit is a fool, short for nitwit

explanation.surface: A stingy idiot nevertheless runs a tidy operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight-knit group is closely bound and well integrated, like a well-ordered community.

clue.text: The first of the Greeks

parts.note: surface reading: the foremost or earliest Greek person, or an instruction to take an initial letter
setter's reading: the letters used by the Greeks, and the wanted one stands at the front of their set

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase looks like an instruction to take the first letter of 'Greeks'; instead it means the first Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha opens the Greek alphabet, the counterpart of our letter A.

clue.text: Greeted a daughter having put on clothes

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies
to dress is to put on clothes

explanation.surface: A girl got dressed before saying hello.
explanation.definitionFit: To address someone is to speak to them directly, so greeted and addressed share a sense.

clue.text: Gem quietly given to nobleman

parts.note: p for piano, the musical direction meaning softly
an earl is a British nobleman

explanation.surface: A jewel is discreetly handed to an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl is a lustrous gem formed inside an oyster shell and set in jewellery.

clue.text: King consumed by entirely personal pride briskly

parts.note: all, as in all alone, means entirely

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed up, so the first item ends up inside the second

parts.note: one's ego is one's self-esteem
R from rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch, eaten up by vanity, strides along briskly.
explanation.walkthrough: R for king comes from Latin rex. Allegro is an Italian musical tempo marking, so it can define an adverb like briskly.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the musical tempo marking meaning at a brisk, lively pace.

clue.text: Sudden overthrow, so pact due to change

indicators.note: to change something is to alter its order, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A treaty is about to be altered, leading to a regime falling suddenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' belongs to the fodder, not the link; without it the letters fall short.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup d'état is a sudden, often violent seizure of government power, toppling the rulers.

clue.text: Appetizers in tin given to ugly people

parts.note: a can is a tin container
apes is an insult for coarse, ugly people

explanation.surface: Party snacks come out of a tin to be handed to unattractive guests.
explanation.definitionFit: Canapés are small savoury bites served before a meal or at drinks parties, a kind of starter.

clue.text: Cook inadequately for likely loser not finishing

indicators.note: not finishing means stopping short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the competitor expected to lose

explanation.surface: A cook does a poor job, as befits a contestant who never finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: To underdo food is to leave it undercooked, not heating it enough.

clue.text: It's twisting or is not twisting

indicators.note: twisting means turning about, so the preceding letters are wrung into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzling riddle over whether something is or is not twisted.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word serves twice: first as the definition, then as the signal to rearrange the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Torsion is the technical term for twisting a body by turning one end against the other.

clue.text: Animated but lined, even wrinkly

indicators.note: something wrinkly is creased out of its smooth shape, so these letters are crumpled into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly face is lively despite being lined and indeed quite wrinkly.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlivened means made lively or brought to life, so it shares the sense of animated.

clue.text: About 54 turned up more depraved

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning
54 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Roughly fifty-four people showed up, an even worse turn of events.
explanation.definitionFit: Viler is the comparative of vile, meaning more wicked or corrupt.

clue.text: Mistake when retired bishop tucked into deer

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the result is read backwards
tucked into means placed inside, so the cleric goes within the animal

parts.note: a roe is a small deer
RR, Right Reverend, is a bishop's title

explanation.surface: A slip occurred when a pensioned-off bishop tucked into venison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired bishop' looks like one phrase, but 'retired' turns round the whole of the deer with the bishop tucked inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, the plain synonym for a wrong act or judgement.

clue.text: Lose control at breakfast? Have a drink!

parts.note: an egg is a typical breakfast item
to flip is to lose one's temper

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper over breakfast and is told to calm down with a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg flip, or eggnog, is a drink of beaten egg with milk, sugar and often spirits.

clue.text: Revoke scientific name held by revolutionary

indicators.note: held by means kept inside, so the preceding letters go within the next word

parts.note: red is a common term for a communist revolutionary
sci is a short form of scientific
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A rebel seizes a Latin species name and cancels it.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescind is to cancel or repeal a law or decision, the same as to revoke it.

clue.text: Letters showing similarity

definitions.meaning: first meaning: mail exchanged between people
second meaning: agreement or match between two things

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests letters that look alike; in fact these are two separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both an exchange of mail and a close match or analogy between things.
